newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Four dead in Czech floods, more rain likely.
newsitem.headline: Four dead in Czech floods, more rain likely.

text.p: Flooding killed four people in the northeast of the Czech Republic as the promise of more rain forced officials to declare a state of emergency, the CTK news agency reported on Monday.
CTK, quoting flood crisis official Ladislav Olejnicka, said two men and two women had died as a result of the flooding.

Jan Havlicek, a spokesman for the town of Sumperk, said the situation was so bad in some areas that families were being forced onto the roofs of their houses as they waited for helicopters to rescue them. "Practically the whole district is underwater," CTK quoted him as saying.
Several hospitals had been cut off due by rising water, while several children's summer camps were evacuated on Monday.
Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus told a news conference on Monday morning that the government was closely monitoring the situation.
Officials said they feared the situation could spread into parts of eastern Bohemia, where tributaries on the upper parts of the Elbe and Upa rivers.
